headline: Burn pECX from BitWindow — and do it before the Alphanet stops.
message: The burn is implemented in BitWindow: on Alphanet, the Receive page carries a Burn Transaction card. Send more than 1,000 pECX to the Bitcoin eater address, and the wallet puts its own first address in the OP_RETURN — that address receives 1/100 of what you burn as real ECX at mainnet, rounded up. The Alphanet is being retired this week, so anyone holding pECX there has to act.

expect.note: Balances may not carry over from alpha to beta.

Ratio and minimum were restated in the same group on 15 Sep ("confirmed that you will get 10 ECX for every 1000 alpha pECX, as long as you burn at least 1000"), and the numbers below were then verified against the implementation itself.
announcement.quote: 1. Send to 1BitcoinEaterDontSendxxx  2. Add a 0-valued op return, to an address A that you have the key for. The coins will go to address A. As long as there is more than the threshold (1000).

published_override.reason: Hand-published on the owner's instruction from the Telegram exports of Drivechain Talk. The source is the project lead in the project's own group plus the wallet implementation, not an official-domain document, so the automated allowlist would refuse it.

spec.network: pECX on the ECX Alphanet — the burn card only exists on Alphanet
spec.ratio: 1/100 of what you burn, rounded up to a whole ECX satoshi: 1,000 → 10 ECX, 1,013 → 10.13 ECX
spec.minimum: Strictly more than 1,000 pECX. Exactly 1,000 is rejected.
spec.deadline: Before the Alphanet stops — expected this week
spec.mainnet: ECX mainnet ~31 October 2026 (BTC block ~973,728); Beta soon after the next BTC difficulty adjustment
spec.payout: The OP_RETURN carries the wallet's own first address, and the ECX credit lands there. BitWindow fills it in — you do not type an address.
spec.source_note: Verified against the implementation: ECXBurnAddress, ECXBurnMinimumSats = 100,000,000,000 sat and ECXCreditSats = ceil(burn/100) in sidechain-orchestrator/wallet/ecx_burn.go. No official document exists.

guide.title: Update BitWindow and switch to Alphanet
guide.detail: The card only appears when the current network is eCash/Alphanet; on any other network it is hidden entirely. LayerTwo ships through Sparkle, not GitHub releases, so update from inside the app.

guide.title: Select an Electrum wallet and unlock it
guide.detail: The burn refuses Core wallets, watch-only wallets and single-sig hardware wallets ("This wallet cannot sign this burn. Select a software wallet with its private key."). Multisig can burn, but only through the CLI with --psbt-out so cosigners can sign.

guide.title: Go to Wallet → Receive
guide.detail: The Burn Transaction card sits under the receive QR on Alphanet. The Claim card on the same page is a different feature for investor keys — don't mix them up.

guide.title: Enter an amount above 1,000
guide.detail: Up to 8 decimals. 1,000 exactly is rejected: "The amount must exceed 1,000.00000000 ECX." There are no increments — the credit is pro-rata, so 1,013 is credited as 10.13 ECX.

guide.title: Read both output panels before signing
guide.detail: "To BitcoinEater" must be your amount to 1BitcoinEaterAddressDontSendf59kuE with 0-value OP_RETURN. The card tells you plainly: "You will receive 1/100 of the amount you burn as real ECX at this address" and "The address used is the first address of this wallet." Don't burn from a wallet whose first address you can't reach later — there is no way to change it in the GUI. The CLI takes no address either.

guide.title: Press Burn Transaction, then keep the txid
guide.detail: BitWindow signs, finalizes and broadcasts, then shows the txid and an explorer link with "Your real ECX credit remains pending." That txid is your proof of burn and your tax record.

guide.title: Prefer a terminal? The same node offers the CLI
guide.detail: drivechain-cli wallet burn-ecx --sats <alphanet-sats>, with --preview to see the transaction without signing, --yes to skip the prompt, and --psbt-in/--psbt-out for multisig. 1,000 pECX = 100,000,000,000 sats, and the amount must exceed it.

warnings: Burning is irreversible. The eater address has no private key by design — those pECX are gone.
You need MORE than 1,000 pECX. Exactly 1,000 is rejected by the wallet, and there is no way to send a top-up to reach the threshold afterwards.
The credit address is the first address of the wallet you burn from. If you cannot sign for that address later, you cannot reach your ECX. There is no field to enter a different one.
If you are burning through the CLI instead of the GUI, the same constraint applies: the OP_RETURN address is derived by the wallet, not chosen by you.
The Alphanet is being retired this week. Anything left on it after it stops is not redeemable — burning is only one of the three options, the others being selling and wrapping.
This came out of a Telegram chat. There is still no official specification document. Verify the numbers against the implementation or ask before moving anything you would miss.
Nobody legitimate needs your seed phrase or private key to help you redeem. Anyone who asks is robbing you.
